findings.suggested_fix: Replace “kamba” with a Kiswahili term for a freshwater crayfish, such as “kaa-mdogo wa maji baridi,” so the animal is not confused with a shrimp/prawn.

findings.source_quote: “Their splashes got bigger and bigger. They were having a lot of fun seeing who could make the biggest splash.”
findings.suggested_fix: Revise these sentences to say that the splashes grew larger and that the girls enjoyed seeing who could make the biggest splash; for example: “Mikupuo ya maji ilizidi kuwa mikubwa. Walifurahia sana kuona ni nani angeweza kutengeneza mkupuo mkubwa zaidi.”
findings.translation_quote: “Maji waliyokuwa wakiyatawanya yalizidi kuwa mengi. Walifurahia sana kuona ni nani angeweza kutapakaza maji mengi zaidi.”

findings.source_quote: “I’m going to tell Mom that you broke the oar.”
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the spacing error: “Nitamwambia Mama kwamba mmevunja kasia.”
Make the reflection explicit, for example: “Mashua ya makasia ikionekana kwenye maji tulivu.”
findings.translation_quote: “Boti ya makasia ikionekana kwenye maji tulivu”

findings.source_quote: “Weathered and broken wooden oars on boards”
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the oars themselves as weathered and broken, rather than describing only their handles; for example: “Makasia ya mbao yaliyochakaa na kuvunjika juu ya mbao.”
findings.translation_quote: “Mikono ya makasia ya mbao iliyochakaa na kuvunjika juu ya mbao”
